Cat food

  • Vet to general
    • 1 — Veterinary/Therapeutic. The brand is strongly positioned around veterinary or clinically oriented nutrition for managing diagnosed health conditions, with therapeutic or veterinary-exclusive diets forming an important part of its identity.
    • 3 — Health/Nutrition Oriented. The brand emphasizes nutritional science or specific health benefits but primarily provides over-the-counter foods for generally healthy cats rather than therapeutic management of diagnosed conditions.

    • 5 — General Wellness/Lifestyle. The brand is primarily positioned around everyday feeding, taste, ingredients, lifestyle, naturalness, convenience, or general wellness rather than veterinary or therapeutic nutrition. General/Non-Therapeutic Nutrition.

  • Science diet to natural
    • Science-Formulated (Nutrient-First): These brands focus strictly on nutrients (proteins, amino acids, vitamins) rather than how appealing the ingredients look to human eyes. They heavily utilize meat by-products, grains, and corn gluten meal because they are highly bioavailable, chemically consistent, and easily enriched with essential synthetic taurine. Examples: Purina ONE, Hill’s Science Diet, and Iams.

    • “Humanized” / Ancestral / Fresh (Ingredient-First): These brands market heavily to the owner’s emotions and dietary trends. They emphasize “real meat as the first ingredient,” grain-free formulations, raw-freeze-dried bits, and the total exclusion of artificial preservatives or by-products. The food looks and sounds like human meals (e.g., “Salmon and Sweet Potato Stew”).

  • Traditional mass market to ultra premium
    • Traditional / Mass-Market Baseline: Dominated by highly processed, ambient dry kibble and budget-friendly grocery store canned pates. The focus is on long shelf-life, bulk affordability, and high palatability (adding fats and flavor coatings so cats find it addictive). Examples: Friskies, 9Lives, and private label supermarket brands.
    • Ultra-Premium Specialized: Focuses on high-moisture formats (pouch broths, minced cuts in gravies, human-grade shreds) or freeze-dried raw food that mimics an obligate carnivore’s natural prey diet. They command luxury pricing and are sold mostly through boutique pet stores or direct subscriptions.

  • I see two clusters: natural/ultra premium and traditional/Science. There is variation within each cluster.
  • Most are general, but two are very much Vet and two are moderate on Vet. I’d say that Vet is a niche. I guess this could be interesting to probe
  • I’m inclined to have a scale with Science_Natural combined with Trad_UltPrem. Keep Vet separate
  • Cat Food Tier (catfoodL_H): Positions cat-food brands from mainstream, widely available, conventional/science-oriented offerings toward higher-priced, specialty, natural and ingredient-focused offerings.
  • Veterinary Focus (VetFocus): Captures the extent to which a cat-food brand specializes in therapeutic diets designed to manage diagnosed health conditions under veterinary guidance.

Boat cruise

  • Vessel Big
    • Low (Small Ships / Yachts / River Boats): Capacity of 50 to 500 guests. Specific Attributes: Highly intimate atmosphere, short or non-existent lines, direct proximity to the water line, and the ability to slide into small, shallow bays, historic river channels, or private islands where mega-ships cannot physically fit. [1, 2, 3]

    • High (Mega Ships / Floating Resorts): Capacity of 3,500 to 7,500+ guests. Specific Attributes: Massive engineering marvels. They feature neighborhood-style floorplans, multi-story open atriums, extensive water parks, roller coasters, theaters, and dozens of distinct bars and restaurants.

  • Service high
    • Low (Mass-Market Density): Staff-to-guest ratio around 1:3 or 1:4; tight space ratios. Specific Attributes: Crowded pool decks, a need to reserve theater seating or dining times weeks in advance, standard cabin sizes, and highly structured, buffet-oriented dining operations.

    • High (Ultra-Luxury Decadence): Staff-to-guest ratio approaching 1:1; massive space-per-guest metrics. Specific Attributes: Free-flowing, open-seating gourmet dining with no reservations required. Living spaces are exclusively multi-room suites with private verandas and dedicated personal butler service.

  • Conventional to expedition
    • 1 — Conventional Leisure Cruising. Primarily visits established tourist ports using fixed itineraries and conventional shore excursions; the cruise experience relies substantially on leisure activities aboard the vessel and conventional tourism ashore.
    • 3 — Destination-Focused Exploration. Destinations and cultural or natural experiences are central to the cruise experience, including smaller or less conventional ports and substantial enrichment or immersion, but itineraries generally rely on established ports and conventional shore access.

    • 5 — Expedition/Basecamp Exploration. The vessel functions as a platform for active exploration of remote environments. Flexible itineraries, expedition teams, small-craft or Zodiac landings, wildlife/nature observation, and access to locations lacking conventional port infrastructure are central to the experience.

  • Family friendly to adults only
    • 1 — Strongly Family/Multigenerational. The brand explicitly targets families traveling with children and provides substantial child/family-specific programming, facilities, entertainment, and accommodations. Disney
    • 3 — General Adult/Multigenerational. The brand welcomes families but neither families with children nor adults seeking a child-free/adult-oriented environment are central to its positioning.
    • 5 — Adults-Only/Strongly Adult-Oriented. The brand either restricts children or is explicitly designed and positioned around an adult experience, with little or no child-oriented programming and an emphasis on adult-oriented atmosphere and activities. Virgin/Viking .

  • Pushing it to two factors, big goes with conventional, service goes with adult only. The factors are highly correlated, so probably not a good idea.

  • Cruise positioning (CruseL_H): Positions cruise lines from large, mainstream, family-oriented resort cruising with conventional ports toward smaller, more intimate, service-intensive, adult-oriented, exploration-focused cruising.

Hiking jacket

  • Everyday to Apline/Technical
    • 1 — Everyday Outdoor / General Recreation. The brand is primarily positioned around everyday outdoor use, casual recreation, travel, or lifestyle apparel rather than demanding technical mountain activities. It may offer performance products, but alpine use is not central to the brand’s positioning. <LI 3 — Performance Outdoor. The brand has a substantial performance orientation and offers apparel designed for serious hiking, backpacking, and demanding outdoor conditions, but its positioning is not predominantly centered on technical alpine pursuits.

    • 5 — Alpine / Highly Technical. The brand is strongly positioned toward mountaineering, climbing, alpinism, or similarly demanding mountain environments. Technical protection, performance, and equipment designed for severe conditions are central to the brand’s identity.

  • Low to high urban
    • 1 — Low Urban/Lifestyle Orientation. The brand is primarily positioned around specialized outdoor or sporting activities, with relatively little emphasis on jackets designed to transition into everyday urban, commuting, travel, or casual use.
    • 3 — Mixed Outdoor/Everyday Orientation. The brand combines performance outdoor apparel with meaningful everyday, travel, or lifestyle use. Its jackets can plausibly serve both outdoor recreation and ordinary daily wear, but urban/lifestyle use is not dominant.

    • 5 — Strong Urban/Lifestyle Orientation. Everyday versatility, comfort, style, and use in urban, commuting, travel, and casual settings are central to the brand’s apparel positioning. Outdoor performance may remain important, but products are deliberately designed and marketed to transition readily into everyday life.

  • Value
    • 1 — Value. The brand is positioned around affordability and accessibility, with much of its jacket assortment priced below specialist premium outdoor brands and distributed broadly to mainstream consumers.
    • 3 — Mid-Market/Premium. The brand occupies the middle of the outdoor-apparel market, offering meaningful performance and quality at prices above value brands but generally below the highest-priced specialist brands.

    • 5 — Premium/High-End. The brand is strongly positioned at the high end of the outdoor-apparel market, with premium pricing central to its market position and substantial use of high-end materials, construction, design, and/or specialized technical capabilities.

  • Sustainability
    • 1 — Limited/Basic. Sustainability is not a substantial part of the brand’s demonstrated operations. There may be general environmental statements or isolated sustainable products, but little evidence of systematic targets, measurement, certified materials, chemical reduction, or circularity.
    • 3 — Credible/Product-Level Commitment. The brand demonstrates meaningful sustainability practices, such as substantial use of recycled/responsibly sourced materials, PFAS reduction, third-party certifications, supply-chain standards, or durability initiatives, but these efforts are not as comprehensive or systemic as those of industry leaders.
    • 5 — Systemic/Industry-Leading. Sustainability is embedded across materials, manufacturing, supply-chain management and product lifecycle. The brand provides transparent quantitative reporting, uses meaningful third-party standards, sets and reports progress toward environmental targets, and has substantial programs addressing materials, chemicals, durability, repair and/or circularity.

  • Go with two factors: sustainability versus the rest (alpha=.91).
  • Jacket Tier (jacketL_H): Positions hiking-jacket brands from value-oriented, everyday/urban and general-recreation use toward premium, highly technical products intended for demanding mountain environments.
  • Sustainability: Captures the extent to which a hiking-jacket brand emphasizes environmental responsibility, responsible materials and production, durability, repairability, and related sustainability values.

Drills

  • 1 — Occasional DIY / Homeowner. Primarily positioned toward homeowners and occasional DIY users performing routine household tasks such as hanging shelves, assembling furniture, and making minor repairs. Emphasizes affordability, simplicity, accessibility, and adequate performance for intermittent use rather than demanding daily use. Examples: Black+Decker, HART, Worx.
  • 3 — Serious DIY / Prosumer. Primarily positioned toward serious DIYers, hobbyists, and users whose demands approach professional use; may also appeal to light-duty professionals such as handymen or property managers. Emphasizes greater durability and performance than basic homeowner tools without being positioned predominantly toward daily trade use. Examples: Ridgid, Craftsman, Skil; perhaps Kobalt.

  • 5 — Professional / Trade. Primarily positioned toward tradespeople, contractors, and other professionals who depend on their tools for frequent or daily work. Emphasizes durability, sustained performance, reliability, and capability under demanding jobsite conditions. Examples: Milwaukee, DeWalt, Makita, Hilti, Festool.

hist(brands$DrillDIY_pro)
  • Goood spread. Many high-end, low end, and some in between
  • User orientation (DrillDIY_pro): Positions cordless-drill brands from occasional homeowner/DIY use to prosumer to frequent professional/trade use under demanding job-site conditions.

Coffee maker

  • Auto to Manual
    • 1 — Highly Automated / Minimal User Control. Brewing is largely automated after the user selects a beverage or initiates the brew. The machine or closed system controls most important brewing variables, requiring little coffee-making skill or intervention.
    • 3 — Moderate User Control. The user makes meaningful choices affecting preparation and extraction, such as grind, dose, brew parameters, or beverage configuration, but substantial portions of the brewing process remain automated. <LI 5 — Highly Manual / Maximum User Control. The user directly controls most important aspects of preparation and extraction, potentially including grind, dose, tamping, temperature, extraction time, pressure or flow, and milk preparation. Achieving consistently high-quality results rewards substantial user skill.
  • Ritual to Convenience
    • 1 — Ritual/Low Convenience. Preparing coffee requires substantial time, attention, and/or hands-on activity. Setup, warm-up, brewing, milk preparation, and cleanup may form an intentional part of the coffee-making experience.
    • 3 — Moderate Convenience. Coffee preparation involves some setup and user involvement but fits readily into an ordinary daily routine. The machine automates substantial portions of preparation while retaining some hands-on steps.

    • 5 — Hyper-Convenience. The machine is designed to minimize time, effort, and cleanup. Coffee can be prepared rapidly with very few user actions, often through one-touch operation, pods/capsules, or highly automated preparation.

  • Drip to Espresso
    • Low (Drip & Filter / Gravity Baselines): Atmospheric pressure extraction. Specific Attributes: Simple heating elements that boil water and drip it over a basket of coffee grounds. Focuses on high-volume, multi-cup carafes (8 to 12 cups) rather than concentrated single shots. [1, 2, 3]
    • High (True Espresso / Pressurized Extraction): 9+ Bars of constant mechanical pressure.

  • BuildGrade cross loads. I guess it could be a third dimension, but let’s not do that now.
  • Barista Involvement (BaristaInvolve): Positions coffee-machine brands from highly automated, convenient preparation requiring little effort or skill toward hands-on preparation emphasizing control, skill, and coffee-making ritual.
  • Brew Focus (Drip_Espresso): Positions coffee-machine brands from primarily drip/filter brewed coffee toward primarily espresso and espresso-based beverages.
